heard: A city-bus-sized asteroid snuck halfway inside our Moon's protective orbit. In February 2023, astronomers at the Canary Islands Telescope spotted the unexpected visitor. Initial estimates showed a rock 40 to 90 meters across, orbiting the Sun every three years. Worse yet, orbital calculations briefly flagged the object as a virtual impactor for March 2026. Alarms spread until further radar tracking completely ruled out any risk, removing it from threat lists. On March 25, the fast-rotating space rock zoomed, safely passed at 175,000 kilometers.
